clue.text: Family fare, fine to some extent

parts.note: to fare is to do, as in 'how did you fare?'
F = fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A menu note: the family meal is reasonably decent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' reads as food beside 'Family'; here it is the verb, meaning to get on or do.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Kind of tired' and 'tired to some extent' say the same thing.

clue.text: Almost exploit rugby team for vast wealth

indicators.note: almost the whole word: its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the British and Irish Lions, a touring rugby team

explanation.surface: Accusing someone of nearly bleeding a rugby side dry to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lions are the combined British and Irish rugby union side that tours every four years.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'making millions' is amassing a fortune, so the plural stands for vast wealth.

clue.text: Look after article in flipping memory

indicators.note: 'in' places the article inside the other word, the way a thing sits in a box
flipping turns the memory over, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone frustrated at having to mind an item stuck in their cursed memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British curse on a bad memory, but it is the instruction to turn the computer memory round.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense: to mother is to care for someone as a parent would, fussing over and tending them.

clue.text: Elevated exercise involving a Biblical character

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read bottom to top
to involve is to include or take in, so the exercise word takes the A into itself

parts.note: to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A lofty workout that somehow features a figure from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: USE with A inside is UASE; read upwards it becomes ESAU, Jacob's brother in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau, who sold his birthright for a bowl of stew, is a character in the Bible.

clue.text: Ready to supply more? Bet sex line will be busy

indicators.note: letters kept busy are set moving and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky wager that a premium-rate chat line will be run off its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a racy bet about a phone line; the question mark flags a playful definition, since something extensible can be stretched to give more.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extensible can be extended, so it stands ready to supply more.

clue.text: Leaving group after ultimately futile sacrifice

indicators.note: the group comes after the letter from 'futile'
ultimately points to the last letter of 'futile'

parts.note: a ring is a group, e.g. a drugs ring

explanation.surface: Someone quitting a band once a pointless sacrifice has been made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Futile sacrifice' reads as one phrase; in fact 'sacrifice' is the definition standing alone at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the religious sense: something given up to a deity.

clue.text: Embargo on articles — fruit?

explanation.surface: A trade ban on certain goods; could fruit be among them?
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the embargo word sits on top of the two articles.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a fruit; the question mark hints at trade embargoes on bananas.

clue.text: Feud: old soldier cheers, welcoming conclusion

indicators.note: the old soldier welcomes the conclusion inside him

parts.note: ta = thanks, as is cheers in British usage

explanation.surface: A veteran toasting the end of a long-running quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' feels like a toast but here means thanks, which is TA in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a bitter, long-running feud.

clue.text: One name I attempt is name of architect

parts.note: N = name; the clue's first 'name', not the one in the definition
have a go = make an attempt

explanation.surface: Someone trying to guess the name of an architect.
explanation.walkthrough: Inigo Jones was the 17th-century English architect behind the Banqueting House in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a first name borne by one famous architect, Jones, so 'name of architect' points to it.

clue.text: Growth of rock, with wind instrument if something in vogue

explanation.surface: A music review: rock music grows as a sax is added to the fashionable sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' and 'wind instrument' suggest music; the definition is botanical, since saxifrage grows in rocky crevices.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxifrage is a plant growing on rocks; its name means rock-breaker.

clue.text: Parliament following party lines? It's just a plaything for Trump's people

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so Parliament's word goes after the party and lines

explanation.surface: A jibe that Parliament toeing the party line is just a toy for Trump's supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party lines' reads as political loyalty, but splits into two pieces. 'Trump's people' are Americans, who use this spelling where the British say dolls' house.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollhouse is the American name for a toy house, a plaything.

clue.text: Eastern light reveals antelope

parts.note: to light (on) is to land, as a bird does

explanation.surface: A dawn glow in the east shows up an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like a noun for sunlight; here it is the verb, to alight or land.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a species name defined by its family, the largest of Africa's antelopes.

clue.text: Supports reverting to stocking sources of wood

indicators.note: to revert is to go back, so the word goes back to front
the forests stock, or hold, the reversed word

explanation.surface: Beams going back into stock, sourced from the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking' may suggest hosiery, fitting with feet, but here it means holding, as a shop stocks goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, plural matching plural: things you prop your feet on are supports.

clue.text: Fruit, green and black, wrapped in small sort of cloth

indicators.note: green and black are wrapped inside the cloth

explanation.surface: A description of fruit in green and black, packed in a little bit of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' is not a colour here but inexperienced; the colour words make the surface sound like a description of the fruit itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a soft red berry, named in its general class.

clue.text: Unsuitable function I recalled hosting President

indicators.note: called back, so the letters go backwards

explanation.surface: An inappropriate event: someone recalls their function playing host to the President.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a party; it is the tangent, TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or ill-fitting.

clue.text: Dismiss the necessary four from Berlin, not five

indicators.note: not five means the letter for five is removed

parts.note: the necessary is slang for money
VIER is German for four; remove V, Roman five

explanation.surface: Firing someone and demanding the required four people from Berlin, not five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The necessary' is British slang for money. To cashier an officer is to dismiss them from the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier someone is to dismiss them, especially from the armed forces.

clue.text: Chromium enduring, not potassium? Suspicious behaviour

indicators.note: not potassium means its symbol is taken out

parts.note: Cr is the chemical symbol for chromium
KEEPING (enduring) minus K, the symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A chemistry lab log with an element missing, and someone acting shiftily.
explanation.walkthrough: Two chemical symbols do the work: Cr is added and K is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun use: sneaking about stealthily is the kind of conduct that looks suspicious.

clue.text: Winter sports vehicle rebuilt in each city

indicators.note: the letters are taken apart and built again in a new order

explanation.surface: A snow vehicle being reconstructed in every city.
explanation.walkthrough: The vehicle-building surface makes 'rebuilt' feel literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice yacht is a sail-powered vehicle on runners that races across frozen lakes.

clue.text: Request acceptable — one may get a flower

parts.note: 'not on' means unacceptable, so on = acceptable

explanation.surface: A polite request is granted, and someone may receive a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not on' is British for unacceptable, so ON stands for acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a garden and houseplant grown for its showy blooms.

clue.text: Trivial political figure, overlooked by a hitman after turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters read upwards
to be overlooked is to have something above you, so in a down clue the hitman letters sit on top

parts.note: A + GUN (a hired gun is a hitman)
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A minor politician kept under watch by an assassin who has shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlooked' reads as ignored, but in a down clue it means sitting below. Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or importance: trivial.

clue.text: Cast out material, completely out of time

indicators.note: every instance of the letter is taken out, not just one

parts.note: T = time; both Ts are removed

explanation.surface: Throwing away fabric that has gone completely out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely' matters: TEXTILE has two Ts, and both must go.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain verb synonym: banishing someone from their homeland drives them away.

clue.text: French very upset following popular addition to magazine?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads upwards

explanation.surface: A Frenchman very put out at a popular magazine supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: An insert is a loose leaflet or supplement slipped into a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine insert is extra material added to it.

clue.text: Something after work? Go with gentleman

parts.note: a knight is a titled gentleman

explanation.surface: Asking what to do after work, and suggesting going out with a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a toilet euphemism for wee. A weeknight is the evening after a working day.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeknight is the evening that follows a working day.

clue.text: Divine females are entering new conveniences

indicators.note: A goes into the conveniences

parts.note: aids are conveniences, things that make life easier
an are is a unit of area; A is its symbol

explanation.surface: Goddesses stepping into brand-new public toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveniences' suggests public toilets; it means AIDS. 'Are' is the metric unit of 100 square metres, abbreviated A.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads are water nymphs of Greek myth, minor female deities.

clue.text: Mostly offensive, wrapped in offensive label

indicators.note: most of the word: the last letter goes
the shortened word is wrapped inside the second offensive

parts.note: the Tet Offensive of 1968 in the Vietnam War
ICKY (offensive, nasty) without its last letter

explanation.surface: A mostly rude remark, wrapped up inside a rude tag.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: first as an adjective (icky), then as a noun (the Tet Offensive).
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the tag tied to goods showing a price or size.

clue.text: Former area supplying Italian food

explanation.surface: An old district that used to provide Italian cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: A short clue built from two standard abbreviations-level pieces: PAST and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the durum-wheat dough behind spaghetti and penne, Italy's signature dish.

clue.text: Self-centred, say, regarding hearing? One's tense inside

parts.note: otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: Someone vain about their hearing, feeling tense inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' suggests speech alongside 'hearing', but it gives EG. OTIC is the medical adjective for the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain adjective synonym: absorbed in oneself and one's own importance.

clue.text: Gemstone? Never picked up unknown quantities

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: Y and X are algebra's unknowns

explanation.surface: A gem, never noticed, of uncertain value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts a sound-alike reading; in a down clue it lifts NO to read ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded stone used in jewellery; the question mark admits it is semi-precious.

clue.text: No railway covers the route initially going from London to Edinburgh?

indicators.note: railway covers, or goes round, the letters

parts.note: RLY is the abbreviation for railway

indicators.note: only the first letter of route is used

explanation.surface: A complaint that no train line runs the length of the London to Edinburgh route.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a rail grumble, and indeed London to Edinburgh is a famous rail route. Edinburgh lies north of London, so the journey is northerly.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling from London to Edinburgh means heading north: a northerly journey.

clue.text: Funeral song to stop incorporating reflection of old King

parts.note: an engine dies when it stops

indicators.note: a reflection shows the letters mirrored, backwards

explanation.surface: A funeral song written to interrupt thoughts about a former king.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the royal cipher of the King Georges, seen on old British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a slow lament sung at a burial, from the Latin 'dirige' opening a service for the dead.
